<a id="page-values"></a>
# Values

How each value type and enum is written, and the records no other page shows. Open it when you need the form of a
value (a color, an alignment, a size, an edge inset) or the words an enum takes.

<a id="values-writing-a-value"></a>
## Writing a value

A key's value is written as on any line: a number; a bare word (an enum's value, `true`, `false`, a color
`#AARRGGBB`, a theme name); a quoted string; JSON for a list or a map; `{expression}` for a value that follows the
state. A value type below is written in its JSON form, bare where that is a number or one word.

In a quoted text `{x}` reads a value, so `"${annual ? 20 : 25}"` is one expression, not a dollar sign before it:
write `"{'$' + (annual ? 20 : 25)}"`. A list with expressions in it is one expression:
`thumbSize={[w, 8]}` (the paint ops' own `rect=[{x},0,10,10]` is the one place an expression sits inside a list).
A key whose value is a variable's name (`measure.variable`, `pan.xVariable`) takes the name quoted:
`measure.variable="pos"`. `drag=lib({l.id})` carries a value; `drag=lib(zz)` reads `zz` as a name.

```notation
Column pad=[16,8,16,8] fill=#FF2563EB radius=8
  Text "x" color=#FFFFFFFF
```

<a id="values-other-spellings-also-read"></a>
## Other spellings (also read)

This reference writes each thing one way, and that is the way to write it. A model often reaches for another
name; the open vocabulary reads these as the word in the third column (a host that reads with the closed vocabulary
says them instead). They are listed so you know them when you read them, not as forms to write.

| Also read | As a | Is | On |
|---|---|---|---|
| `disabled=` | key | `enabled=` negated | any line |
| `readonly=` | key | `readOnly=` | any line |
| `disabled` | flag | `enabled=false` | any line |
| `readonly` | flag | `readOnly` | any line |

<a id="values-value-types"></a>
## Value types

<a id="type-Alignment"></a>
### Alignment

Written: [x, y] from -1 to 1, or a name: topLeft, topCenter, topRight, centerLeft, center, centerRight, bottomLeft, bottomCenter, bottomRight.

Flutter's `Alignment`: -1 (start) to 1 (end) per axis. JSON: `[x, y]`.

<a id="type-AxisPosition"></a>
### AxisPosition

Written: a number (distance from the start) or {"start": d}, {"end": d}, {"start": a, "end": b}, {"align": -1..1}, {"relative": d}.

Where a child of a freeform (stack) parent sits on one axis, as Flutter's `Positioned` or `Align`, in the parent's padded box:

<a id="type-AxisSize"></a>
### AxisSize

Written: a number (fixed) or {"fill"|"flexible"|"hug"|"fixed": number}.

Sizing along one axis. `value` is the design size: the size for `SizeFit.fixed`, and the fallback whenever a mode can't apply. JSON: a number (fixed) or `{"fill"|"flexible"|"hug": value}`.

<a id="type-BorderRadius"></a>
### BorderRadius

Written: a number (every corner), [x, y] (every corner elliptical) or [topLeft, topRight, bottomRight, bottomLeft] (each a number or [x, y]).

Flutter's `BorderRadius`: four corners, each circular or elliptical. JSON (sparse, see `fromJson`): `8`, `[16, 8]` or `[8, [16, 8], 0, 0]`.

<a id="type-BoxConstraints"></a>
### BoxConstraints

Written: {"minWidth", "maxWidth", "minHeight", "maxHeight"} (each optional, numbers >= 0).

Flutter's `BoxConstraints`, where a missing bound means unconstrained.

<a id="type-Color"></a>
### Color

Written: "#AARRGGBB" or "#RRGGBB" (hex, alpha first).

A 32-bit ARGB color, as Flutter's `Color`. JSON: `"#AARRGGBB"` (`"#RRGGBB"` and ints also read), or the name of one of the project's theme colors (`"ember"`: `ThemeTokens.colors`, resolved before the document renders; see `resolveThemeRefs`).

<a id="type-EdgeInsets"></a>
### EdgeInsets

Written: a number (all sides), [horizontal, vertical] or [left, top, right, bottom].

Flutter's `EdgeInsets` (left, top, right, bottom). JSON: a number (all sides), `[horizontal, vertical]` or `[left, top, right, bottom]`.

<a id="type-FontFeature"></a>
### FontFeature

Written: an OpenType tag ("tnum", "ss01") or "tag=value" ("liga=0").

<a id="type-FontWeight"></a>
### FontWeight

Written: 100, 200 ... 900.

<a id="type-IconData"></a>
### IconData

Written: a Material icon name ("check_circle", "lock_open_rounded"), an image URL, or {"type": "MATERIAL_ICON", "name", "style"}.

<a id="type-Offset"></a>
### Offset

Written: [dx, dy].

An offset. JSON: `[dx, dy]`.

<a id="type-Rect"></a>
### Rect

Written: [left, top, width, height].

<a id="type-Size"></a>
### Size

Written: [width, height].


<a id="values-enums"></a>
## Enums

An enum's value is a bare word: `textAlign=center`, `overflow=ellipsis`.

<a id="enum-AnimateCommand"></a>
### AnimateCommand

| Word | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `forward` | `forward(from:)`: plays to the end; on a variable, carries on toward `AnimateAction.target` (from where it is, or from `AnimateAction.from`). |
| `reverse` | `reverse(from:)`: plays back to the start. |
| `toggle` | Forward when at (or heading to) the start, else back. |
| `repeat` | `repeat()`, as the animation's own `NodeAnimation.repeat` says (forever when it says nothing). |
| `stop` | `stop()`: holds where it is. |
| `reset` | `reset()`: back to the start, stopped. |
| `animateTo` | `animateTo(target)`: from where it is to `AnimateAction.target` (0–1; on a variable, any number) over `AnimateAction.duration`. |
| `animateBack` | `animateBack(target)`. |
| `set` | `value = target`: jumps there; a running animation carries on from it. |

<a id="enum-ChartGridLineMode"></a>

| Word | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `centered` | How a series chart places its grid lines (and solid reference lines). `centered`: centered on the value's rounded y (the bottom line one pixel row up, inside the plot); a 1 px line there straddles two pixel rows. `crisp` (the default): whole pixel rows from the value's rounded y down (the bottom line's up, inside the plot), so a line of whole width is sharp; other widths stay centered on the value. `exact`: the rows just above the value's unrounded y, like a Flutter box of that height whose bottom edge sits at the value (sharp when that is a whole pixel, soft otherwise). |

| `exact` | How a series chart places its grid lines (and solid reference lines). `centered`: centered on the value's rounded y (the bottom line one pixel row up, inside the plot); a 1 px line there straddles two pixel rows. `crisp` (the default): whole pixel rows from the value's rounded y down (the bottom line's up, inside the plot), so a line of whole width is sharp; other widths stay centered on the value. `exact`: the rows just above the value's unrounded y, like a Flutter box of that height whose bottom edge sits at the value (sharp when that is a whole pixel, soft otherwise). |

<a id="enum-HeroFlies"></a>
### HeroFlies

| Word | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `betweenScreens` | While a navigation plays, from its place on the screen that goes to its place on the screen that comes, when both have the tag (Flutter's `Hero`). |
| `inPlace` | When it appears, from where the node with its tag was a moment ago (a node hidden or removed in the last two seconds, a dropped drag copy, a node on a screen that is closing): a picked emoji flying from its picker to its chip. Flutter's `Hero` has no such trigger (the `local_hero` package's `LocalHero` is the nearest). Heroes that fly in place find each other only. |
| `lift` | Lifted out of another node's place: when it comes on screen while another node with its tag is shown (on the same screen, on a screen or an overlay under it), it flies from that node's place to its own, drawn above everything (an overlay's backdrop too), and the node it left keeps its place hidden (a gap) while it is shown. When it goes (its overlay closes, it is removed, its tag changes) it flies back to that node, which shows again as it lands. Both ends are followed while it flies (a list that scrolls); a place that is gone is flown to where it was last seen, fading. Timed by `HeroTag.flight`'s `duration` and `curve` (the way back plays the curve backward), else 300 ms; with reduced motion it does not fly. A long-pressed bubble to its menu, a photo to its viewer, a row to a sheet. Lifted heroes find each other only. |

| `arc` | Along a curve (Material's arc), turning upright as it lands, with a halo in the color of its first drop shadow (soft white without one). |
| `morph` | Both nodes fly fitted to the box in between, the leaving one fading out as the arriving one fades in, corners morphing. |
| `fadeThrough` | `morph`, the leaving node gone over the first 35% (Material fade through). |
| `containerTransform` | Material container transform: a card grows into a whole screen (tag the card and the destination's root the same); the card fades out over the first 30%. |

It slides in (or as its `OpenModalAction.routeTransition`'s enter side says), a swipe toward its edge dismisses it when `OpenModalAction.barrierDismissible`, `OpenModalAction.closeAfterMs` closes it by itself, and its screen closes it with a `CloseModalAction`. <a id="enum-TriggerType"></a>
### TriggerType

| Word | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `click` | A tap (a click with a mouse). `${result}` holds where it landed (`x`, `y` in the node, `globalX`, `globalY`) and the modifier keys held (`meta`, `shift`, `alt`). |
| `doubleTap` | Two taps in quick succession. A node with double tap reactions waits out the double tap timeout before its single taps run. |
| `longPress` | A long press: the platform's (500 ms), or held for `Trigger.holdMs` when it is set; `Trigger.commitMs` and `Trigger.haptic` as for hold. |
| `hold` | A press held for `Trigger.holdMs`; letting go early cancels it (before `Trigger.commitMs`, when set). |
| `secondaryClick` | A right click, or a two-finger tap on a trackpad (`${result.x}`, `${result.y}`: where, on screen). |
| `pointerDown` | A pointer went down on the node. |
| `pointerUp` | A pointer went up on the node, or was cancelled (taken away by the system or a scroll): `${result.cancelled}` says which (`onPointerUp={result.cancelled ? close : pick}`), `${result.x}`, `${result.y}` where, in the node. |
| `hover` | The mouse cursor moved over the node (fires when it enters, too). |
| `cursorEnter` | The mouse cursor entered the node (once). |
| `cursorExit` | The mouse cursor left the node (once). |
| `swipeLeft` | A swipe (a fling) to the left, right, up or down. |
| `swipeRight` |  |
| `swipeUp` |  |
| `swipeDown` |  |
| `drag` | The node is dragged (every move); `dragEnd` when it's let go (`${result.vx}`, `${result.vy}`: its speed; `${result.cancelled}`: the drag was taken away, not let go). |
| `dragEnd` |  |
| `wheel` | Wheel or trackpad scroll over the node (`${result.deltaX}`, `${result.deltaY}`, and where: `${result.x}`, `${result.y}` in the node). |
| `pinch` | A pinch on the node: two fingers on a touch screen, or a trackpad (ctrl + wheel on the web). Each step fires it with `${result.scale}`, the scale of that step (multiply a zoom by it), and the point it is about, `${result.x}`, `${result.y}` in the node (between the fingers; the pointer on a trackpad): zoom about it by keeping that point still. |
| `changed` | An input's value changed (typed text, a toggled checkbox, a slider step, a picked item). `${result}` is the new value (a text field's: its text, word and selection). |
| `changeEnd` | A slider was let go, with its final value. |
| `changeStart` | A slider was taken (a drag or a press on it began, or a key moves it), with its value before the change (Flutter's `onChangeStart`). |
| `submitted` | A text field was submitted from the keyboard. |
| `deleted` | An input chip's delete icon was tapped, or Delete or Backspace pressed on it (Flutter's `onDeleted`). |
| `editingComplete` | A text field lost focus after editing. |
| `focusGained` | A text field gained or lost focus. |
| `focusLost` |  |
| `load` | A screen appeared (set on its canvas). |
| `imageLoading` | A node's image fill started loading, became ready, or failed. `${result.url}` identifies the image and `${result.status}` is `loading`, `loaded`, or `error`. Cached images can report loaded immediately without a loading event. |
| `imageLoaded` |  |
| `imageError` |  |
| `backPressed` | On a screen (its canvas): the user tried to leave it (the system or browser back button, a back gesture, Escape on a dialog) while the canvas's `blockBack` holds (`props.blockBack`, usually bound: `${= dirty}`). The screen stays and these actions run instead, e.g. a "Discard changes?" confirm that leaves with a navigate pop, which the block doesn't stop. While `blockBack` is false, back leaves as usual and this doesn't fire. |
| `valueChanged` | Variable `Trigger.variable` changed while the screen shows. |
| `timer` | Every `Trigger.intervalMs` while the screen shows (`Timer.periodic`) and `Trigger.when` holds; `${result.tick}` counts. |
| `frame` | Every frame while the node is on stage and `Trigger.when` holds (a `Ticker`): `${result.dt}` (ms since the tick this chain last got), `${result.elapsed}` (ms since it started), `${result.frame}`. A frame that comes while the chain still runs is skipped; its time goes to the next `dt`. A design canvas never ticks. |
| `keyDown` | A key went down (or up) while the screen shows; `Trigger.key` limits it to one key or combination, `Trigger.when` to while a formula holds. `${result.key}`, `${result.shift}`, `${result.alt}`, `${result.meta}`. |
| `keyUp` |  |
| `scroll` | The node (a scrolling row, column, list, grid or canvas) scrolled (`${result.offset}`, `${result.max}`, `${result.fraction}` 0–1, `${result.index}` the item at the start of the view (the last at the end), `${result.count}` the items, `${result.overscroll}` how far it is pulled past an end: below 0 past the start, above 0 past the end, 0 within). Store what a carousel's arrows, dots or progress bar show. How near the end it is, to load more: `${result.max - result.offset}` (under 600: fetch the next page); a list's `pagination` loads its next page by itself (`thresholdPixels`). |
| `scrollEnd` | The node stopped scrolling; `${result}` as for `scroll`. |
| `enterViewport` | At least `Trigger.visibleFraction` of the node became visible (and stayed so for `Trigger.visibleMs`), or it fell below that after being visible. With `Trigger.onceKey` (`${item.id}`), an impression: once per item per app session. |
| `exitViewport` |  |
| `dragStart` | Drag and drop: on a draggable (start, cancel, completed) and on a drop target (drop, enter, exit, rejected). `${result}` and `${drag}` hold the drag (what was dragged is `${result.data}`). A list with a `reorder` fires `dragStart` when a row is picked up and `dragCompleted` when it is let go (moved or not), with `${result.index}` and `${result.item}`: a list can change while a row is lifted (fold its rows into tiles). On a node with a `drag` reaction (and no drag and drop), `dragStart` is the start of that one-finger drag, where the finger went down (`${drag.x}`, `${drag.y}`): begin a stroke there rather than on `pointerDown`, which fires for every finger of a pinch. |
| `dragCancel` |  |
| `dragCompleted` |  |
| `drop` |  |
| `dragEnter` |  |
| `dragExit` |  |
| `dropRejected` |  |
| `reorder` | A data list row was dragged to a new place by this node, its reorder handle (`${result.from}`, `${result.to}`). A list with a `reorder` fires it too, with `${result.item}`, `${result.fromList}`, `${result.toList}`. |
| `refresh` | A list or grid was pulled past its start to refresh (its `pullToRefresh`, or its pagination's); its pagination reloads its first page too. A list with this reaction can always be pulled. |
| `swipeAction` | A swipe action of a list item ran (the list's `swipeActions`): `${result.action}`, `${result.label}`, `${result.item}`, `${result.index}`. |
| `rowTap` | A table view's body row was tapped: `${result.row}` (the row's data), `${result.rowIndex}`, `${result.column}` (the tapped column's key), `${result.columnIndex}`. |
| `sort` | A table header was activated by pointer or keyboard: `${result.column}` is its key, `${result.columnIndex}` its index, and `${result.ascending}` the new direction. |
| `linkTap` | A link in a text was tapped: a run of its `runs` with a `link` (`TextRun.link`). `${result.link}` is the run's link, `${result.text}` its characters, `${result.start}` and `${result.end}` where they are in the text. Without this reaction the tap opens the link (a web page, `mailto:`, `tel:`, an app link), as `openLink` does; with it, its actions run instead (a run whose link names something of the app's own: `link="restart"`). |
| `actionError` | On the current canvas: a failed action chain or cloud subscription. `${result.error}` is `{type, message, action, nodeId}` (no stack or raw service objects). A failure in this reaction reports to the host without recursively firing another actionError reaction. |
| `event` | On a component call: the component fired its event `Trigger.event` (a `componentEvent` action inside its definition); `${result}` is the event's payload. Flutter: the callback passed to a widget's `onChanged`-style parameter. The handler runs in the caller's scope. |

<a id="values-records"></a>
## Records

<a id="type-AnimationRepeat"></a>
### AnimationRepeat

`controller.repeat(reverse:, count:)`. `count` 0 repeats forever; a count ends at the end of its last run. JSON: `{}` (forever), `{"reverse": true, "count": 3}`; `true` and a bare count read too.

A record: written whole as JSON (`key={…}`), or field by field as dotted keys under the key that holds it (`key.field=…`).

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `reverse` | `true`/`false` | `false` |  |
| `count` | whole number (≥ 0) | `0` | 0: forever. |

<a id="type-AnimationTrack"></a>
### AnimationTrack

One tween a `NodeAnimation` drives: a property at a binding `path` of a node, or a `variable`.

A record: written whole as JSON (`key={…}`), or field by field as dotted keys under the key that holds it (`key.field=…`).

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | text | `""` | Stable within its animation, so an edit can address it (`animations.enter.tracks.fade.from`). Optional. |
| `path` | text | `""` | A binding path (`motion.rotate`, `opacity`, `decoration.fills[0].color`). |
| `node` | text | `""` | The target node's id or key; empty: the node the animation is on. |

<a id="type-ClipCut"></a>
### ClipCut

A shape cut out of a node at a point of its box (`Decoration.clipCuts`), in the node's own pixels whatever its size, so a ticket's notch stays a round 12 px however the ticket grows: a circle of `radius` centered at `center`, or SVG path data `d` with its origin there.

A record: written whole as JSON (`key={…}`), or field by field as dotted keys under the key that holds it (`key.field=…`).

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `center` | [Alignment](#type-Alignment) | `[0,0]` | The point of the box it sits at, an alignment (`"centerLeft"`, `[1, 0]`): a circle's center, a path's origin. |
| `radius` | number (≥ 0) |  | A circle of this radius in pixels. |
| `d` | text |  | SVG path data in pixels, its (0, 0) at `center`. |

<a id="type-Flight"></a>
### Flight

How a hero that flies in place (`HeroFlies.inPlace`) flies in from where the node with its tag was: on a spring by default (the node's `motion` transition's, when it has one with a spring), or, with a `duration`, along a curve that rises `lift` (or `liftShare` of the distance, the larger) above the higher end (as Flutter's `MaterialRectArcTween` bends a hero's path), swelling to `swell` at the middle and spinning `turns` times (toward the way it flies), trailing `trail` fading dots.

A record: written whole as JSON (`key={…}`), or field by field as dotted keys under the key that holds it (`key.field=…`).

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `duration` | whole number (≥ 0) | `0` | 0: on the node's spring. |
| `curve` | [AnimationCurve](#enum-AnimationCurve) | `easeInOut` |  |
| `lift` | number | `0` | Rise of the path's control point above the higher end (px). |
| `liftShare` | number | `0` | The same as a share of the distance flown (the larger wins). |
| `swell` | number (≥ 0) | `1` | Scale at the middle of the flight. |
| `turns` | number | `0` | Turns over the flight, clockwise when flying right. |
| `trail` | whole number (≥ 0) | `0` | Fading dots left behind. |
| `trailColor` | [Color](#type-Color) | `#FFFFC83D` |  |

<a id="type-GesturePhysics"></a>
### GesturePhysics

How a node moves on its own once the pointer lets go, the same for a `DragMotion`, a `DragSource`'s return and a `TransformGesture`: a fling that slows by `friction` (Flutter's `FrictionSimulation`), a stretch of `overscroll` past the bounds, and a `spring` onto the `snap` target nearest to where the fling would stop.

A record: written whole as JSON (`key={…}`), or field by field as dotted keys under the key that holds it (`key.field=…`).

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spring` | [Spring](#type-Spring) | `{}` | The spring it settles on. |
| `fling` | `true`/`false` | `true` | Whether a release keeps the pointer's velocity and coasts. |
| `friction` | number (≥ 0, ≤ 1) | `0.865` | The share of a fling's speed lost per second. |
| `minFlingVelocity` | number | `50` | Pixels per second: slower releases don't fling; the fastest start. |
| `maxFlingVelocity` | number | `8000` | Pixels per second: slower releases don't fling; the fastest start. |
| `overscroll` | number (≥ 0, ≤ 1) | `0.5` | How far it stretches past its bounds (0 a hard stop, 1 free). |
| `snap` | [GestureSnap](#type-GestureSnap) |  |  |

<a id="type-Spring"></a>
### Spring

Flutter's `SpringDescription`: either the physical triple (`SpringDescription(mass:, stiffness:, damping:)`, when `stiffness` and `damping` are both given) or `SpringDescription.withDurationAndBounce` (`duration` ms, `bounce`). The one spring value of the model: transitions, animations, gestures, a flip card's settle and a route's dismiss all take it. JSON: `{"stiffness": 380, "damping": 36}` or `{"duration": 500, "bounce": 0.3}` (sparse; `{}` is `withDurationAndBounce()`'s defaults).

A record: written whole as JSON (`key={…}`), or field by field as dotted keys under the key that holds it (`key.field=…`).

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `stiffness` | number |  | The physical spring's constants; both null: `duration` and `bounce`. |
| `damping` | number |  | The physical spring's constants; both null: `duration` and `bounce`. |
| `mass` | number | `1` |  |
| `duration` | whole number (≥ 1) | `500` | `withDurationAndBounce`: ms, and 0 (none) to 1. |
| `bounce` | number | `0` |  |

<a id="type-TransformHandles"></a>
### TransformHandles

On-canvas handles that make a node an editable object (a sticker, a collage): corners scale it, edges stretch it, a knob rotates it.

A record: written whole as JSON (`key={…}`), or field by field as dotted keys under the key that holds it (`key.field=…`).

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `corners` | `true`/`false` | `true` |  |
| `edges` | `true`/`false` | `false` | Edge handles stretch one axis (`TransformGesture.scaleXVariable`...); hidden with `aspectLock`. |
| `rotateKnob` | `true`/`false` | `true` |  |
| `snapAngle` | number | `0` | Degrees the knob snaps to; 0 is free. |
| `aspectLock` | `true`/`false` | `true` | Corner handles keep the aspect ratio. |
| `minWidth` | number | `16` | The drawn size's limits (0 max: none). |
| `minHeight` | number | `16` | The drawn size's limits (0 max: none). |
| `maxWidth` | number | `0` | 0 for no limit. |
| `maxHeight` | number | `0` | The drawn size's limits (0 max: none). |
| `outline` | `true`/`false` | `true` | A selection outline around the box. |
| `color` | [Color](#type-Color) | `#FF2F80ED` |  |
| `handleSize` | number | `12` | A handle's size; its touch target is at least 32. |
| `selectionVariable` | text | `""` | A text variable holding the selected object's key: handles show only while it equals `selectionKey` (empty: the node's id), and a tap writes it. Empty: handles always show. |
| `selectionKey` | text | `""` | A text variable holding the selected object's key: handles show only while it equals `selectionKey` (empty: the node's id), and a tap writes it. Empty: handles always show. |

<a id="type-TransitionReveal"></a>
### TransitionReveal

A clip that reveals a screen as a transition plays: a circle or rectangle growing from `origin` until it covers the screen.

A record: written whole as JSON (`key={…}`), or field by field as dotted keys under the key that holds it (`key.field=…`).

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `shape` | `circle` `rect` | `circle` |  |
| `origin` | `tap` `node` `center` `point` | `tap` |  |
| `x` | number | `0` | `RevealOrigin.point`: the alignment, -1 to 1. |
| `y` | number | `0` | `RevealOrigin.point`: the alignment, -1 to 1. |
| `startRadius` | number | `0` | The radius (half size, for a rect) it starts at. |

<a id="type-TransitionSide"></a>
### TransitionSide

How one screen moves during a `RouteTransition`: an entering screen starts at `motion` and comes to rest; a leaving one starts at rest and ends at `motion` (a `Pose`: a transform, `shiftX`/`shiftY` in screen sizes, with an opacity and a blur); this side's `curve`, `delayMs` and `durationMs` time it inside the route's duration.

A record: written whole as JSON (`key={…}`), or field by field as dotted keys under the key that holds it (`key.field=…`).

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `motion` | [Pose](#type-Pose) | `{}` | The values it moves from (entering) or to (leaving). |
| `reveal` | [TransitionReveal](#type-TransitionReveal) |  |  |
| `curve` | [AnimationCurve](#enum-AnimationCurve) | `fastOutSlowIn` |  |
| `delayMs` | whole number (≥ 0) | `0` | Milliseconds into the transition this side starts. |
| `durationMs` | whole number |  | Null: to the end. |

<a id="type-VisualDensity"></a>
### VisualDensity

Flutter's `VisualDensity`.

A record: written whole as JSON (`key={…}`), or field by field as dotted keys under the key that holds it (`key.field=…`).

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `horizontal` | number (≥ -4, ≤ 4) | `0` |  |
| `vertical` | number (≥ -4, ≤ 4) | `0` |  |

<a id="type-Wave"></a>
### Wave

A sine added to a track's value: `amplitude * sin(2π(cycles·t + phase))`, fading by `1 − decay·t` (a shake dies out with decay 1), folded to its absolute value with `rectify` (a ball's hops). Flutter has no counterpart; a list of them is a Fourier series: a wobble, a sway, a flame's flicker.

A record: written whole as JSON (`key={…}`), or field by field as dotted keys under the key that holds it (`key.field=…`).

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cycles` | number | `1` |  |
| `amplitude` | number | `1` |  |
| `phase` | number | `0` |  |
| `decay` | number | `0` |  |
| `rectify` | `true`/`false` | `false` |  |
